summary: Global semiconductor equipment billings hit a record $36.6B in Q1 2026 (+14% YoY), and SEMI's July mid-year forecast raised 2026 equipment sales to a record $165.9B (+23% YoY). DRAM equipment spending is projected up 39% on HBM buildouts — a strongly expansionary capital cycle for test demand.

The four largest hyperscalers plan roughly $725B of 2026 capex (+77% YoY), with ~75% tied directly to AI infrastructure; capacity remains supply-constrained. Compute and system-level test demand continues to outrun supply, supporting Zenith and Nexus family upside.
sources: [Futurum: AI Capex 2026](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/ai-capex-2026-the-690b-infrastructure-sprint/) ; [FactSet: hyperscaler capex vs cash flow](https://insight.factset.com/hyperscalers-tap-external-financing-as-ai-capex-outruns-cash-flow)

summary: Automotive semiconductor demand remains weak with recovery expectations sliding to 2027; distributor inventory has normalized but auto customers lack the confidence to restock. Tariff negotiations keep the 2026 demand range unusually wide — expect continued push-out risk from automotive accounts.

US manufacturing PMI slipped to 53.8 in July, a four-month low though still expansionary; future-output expectations are at an eight-month low and supplier delivery times are deteriorating sharply amid Middle East conflict. Industrial test demand is stabilizing but not yet recovering.

Q2 2026 smartphone shipments fell 4% YoY and IDC forecasts a 13.9% full-year decline as the memory shortage pushes component costs up sharply. Mobile test demand faces both weaker units and customers redeploying rather than expanding capacity.

Mature-node excess inventory from 2023-25 has largely cleared and distributor stock is back to normal, but automotive customers are not restocking. Memory makers have pivoted capacity to HBM (sold out for 2026), supporting memory-test investment even as consumer segments stay cautious.

Teradyne reported a record Q2 on July 29 with revenue of $1.33B and ~70% of revenue AI-related, and test equipment is running ~8% of total semiconductor capex year-to-date. Peer results validate a multi-year test-demand expansion, though competition for AI compute test sockets is intensifying.

Advanced-AI chip exports to China now run under case-by-case licensing with volume caps and security testing; a Commerce datacenter-chip classification review due July 1 could trigger further measures. A portion of China-bound backlog carries license-timing risk.

High-performance semiconductors carry an additional 25% Section 232 tariff since January, and a hard June 2027 deadline sets up escalation to rates as high as 100% on Chinese-made semiconductors. Component landed-cost and purchase-price-variance pressure builds over the next two quarters.

Global manufacturing remains in expansion with new orders near a four-year peak, but momentum is fading and supply-chain pressure from the Middle East conflict is the worst in nearly four years. The macro backdrop supports the plan without providing upside cushion.
